tagline: The dive capital of the Caribbean — a marine-park island where low-wake, zero-emission boats aren't a luxury, they're the conservation mandate.
summary: Bonaire is the smallest and easternmost of the ABC islands, a flat, arid diving destination whose entire coastline is a protected marine park (Bonaire National Marine Park, established 1979). It drew a record 182,181 stay-over visitors in 2024 and roughly 359,000 cruise passengers — a tourism base built almost entirely on the reef. That conservation identity makes Bonaire an unusually strong fit for silent, zero-wake foiling: the island's regulators and dive-led visitor economy actively penalize the noise, fumes and wake of conventional boats. Today shore-dive shuttles, Klein Bonaire transfers and resort runs use diesel craft; there is no electric or foiling tier. For Ocean Whisperer, Bonaire is a roadmap (scale-vision) market reached from Curaçao — the first proof that one premium standard travels island-to-island across the Dutch Caribbean.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II's silent, zero-wake operation is uniquely aligned with Bonaire's marine-park mandate — the short shore-dive and Klein Bonaire hops are squarely in range, and the ~38 nm Curaçao link sits at the longer-range edge of the platform.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Not required for Bonaire's intra-island work; relevant only if the Dutch-Caribbean network later extends to the longer Aruba reaches.

competitive_landscape: Diesel dive boats, water taxis and a single inter-island turboprop serve Bonaire today. There is no electric or foiling water tier. Bonaire's conservation rules and dive-led audience make it actively hostile to noisy, high-wake operation — a structural advantage for a silent foiling entrant.
seasonality: Bonaire sits below the main hurricane belt with calm leeward water year-round, supporting near-continuous operation. The dive economy runs all year, with peak stay-over demand in the Dec–Apr northern-winter window.
regulatory_note: Bonaire is a special municipality of the Netherlands (Caribbean Netherlands). The entire coastline falls under STINAPA's Bonaire National Marine Park, which strictly regulates vessel operation, mooring and wake — rules that favor zero-emission, low-wake vessels.
